chunks: And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Humran, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrating.

He said: 'Al-mubar'ah (separation by mutual consent) becomes clear from its hour without divorce, and there is no inheritance between them, because the bond of marriage (ismah) has separated from them at the moment that occurred from her and from the husband.'

key_terms.اَلْمُبَارَأَةُ: Mutual separation or release from marital bond

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between mubar'ah and divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that al-mubar'ah is a distinct legal mechanism from talaq, taking effect immediately upon declaration to sever the marital bond. This immediate separation precludes mutual inheritance, as the 'immunity' (ismah) from marital obligations is established at that precise moment. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between divorce and mutual separation, emphasizing the instantaneous nature of the bond's dissolution.
